info.title: Job Application Tracker API
info.description: Job Application Tracker API with Better Auth email/password authentication. Better Auth is mounted at /api/auth and resource routes at /api/v1. Browser requests authenticate through Better Auth's session cookie; the optional Bearer scheme requires enabling the Better Auth Bearer plugin and represents a Better Auth session token, not necessarily a JWT. Every application/resume operation requires a valid session, a verified email, and resource ownership. Registration sends a verification email without creating a login session; the first successful email verification automatically establishes a session. Unverified users cannot sign in or access business features. Registration, sign-in, email verification and resending, password recovery (including its email-link callback), and the session-check endpoint remain callable without a session. Verification email delivery requires emailVerification.sendVerificationEmail; reset email delivery requires emailAndPassword.sendResetPassword. Verification and password-reset credentials each expire 900 seconds after issuance; this does not define the session lifetime. Issuing a replacement credential invalidates all earlier credentials for the same user and purpose, without invalidating credentials for the other purpose. Latest-credential enforcement requires project-specific backend state and atomic issuance/validation beyond Better Auth's default email-link behavior. A successful password reset consumes its credential and revokes every existing session for the user, without automatically signing them in. Protected operations must check authoritative session validity so revoked sessions are not accepted through stale caches. Use Better Auth's CSRF protections and trusted origins for cookie-authenticated requests. AI Copilot contracts follow PRD 1.4, AI_Design.md, and Database_Design.md 1.4. AI operations require the same authoritative session, verified-email, and ownership checks. These contracts describe planned behavior, not deployed endpoints; explicitly marked retry and failure-policy proposals remain subject to the listed decisions.

tags.name: Better Auth
tags.description: Better Auth built-in email/password, user and session operations.

tags.name: AI Copilot
tags.description: Application-bound workspaces, independent conversations, saved material provenance, and streamed generation. Base materials are loaded by backend code on every turn; the model is never offered a material tool. Navigation and blank-conversation creation never invoke the model or read materials into a conversation.

post.description: Registers with email and password and sends a verification email. Registration does not create a login session or issue a login-session cookie; the response token is null and the user must verify their email before signing in or accessing business features. The verification credential expires 900 seconds after issuance and is superseded by any later verification credential for that user. Configure emailAndPassword.enabled=true, emailAndPassword.requireEmailVerification=true, emailAndPassword.autoSignIn=false, and emailVerification.sendOnSignUp=true with a working emailVerification.sendVerificationEmail callback. With email enumeration protection, an already-registered email may also receive a generic success response; this response is not proof that a new account was created.

200.description: Registration accepted without creating a login session. Await email verification; the token is null. A generic response may also be returned for an already-registered email.

post.summary: Sign in with email and password
post.description: Signs in a user with a verified email and valid email/password credentials. On success, the server establishes a session in an HttpOnly cookie. An unverified email cannot obtain a session and is rejected with 403 EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED. The frontend may offer the send-verification-email action; requesting a new verification email supersedes that user's earlier verification links.

403.description: Email is not verified (EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED), or the request origin is not trusted. No login session is created.

post.description: Invalidates the current Better Auth session and clears its session cookie.

401.description: Authentication is required or session is invalid.

get.description: Returns user and session for a valid cookie (or supported bearer session). When not signed in, or when the session has expired or been revoked, returns HTTP 200 with null. This endpoint is intentionally callable without credentials. Registration creates no session, so clients remain signed out until successful email verification. After verification, use this endpoint to load the automatically established session. After a successful password reset, every previously issued session is invalid; session checks must not accept stale cached credentials.

200.description: Current session and user, or null if signed out.

post.description: Button-triggered sending or resending of a verification link, using emailVerification.sendVerificationEmail. Registration also sends a verification email automatically. No signed-in session is required. Each issued verification credential expires after 900 seconds. Issuing a replacement invalidates all earlier verification credentials for that user, while leaving password-reset credentials unaffected. This latest-only rule requires project-specific backend state and atomic checks; it is not guaranteed by Better Auth's default signed verification links. For anonymous requests, a successful response does not disclose whether the email exists or is already verified and does not guarantee that a message was sent. With a session, the email must match the current unverified user. The email link opens GET /api/auth/verify-email. Resend cooldown and rate-limit values are not specified by this contract.

200.description: Request accepted without disclosing anonymous account existence or verification status.

400.description: Invalid input, verification email delivery is not configured, or the signed-in user's email does not match or is already verified.

403.description: The request origin or callback URL is not trusted.

429.description: The configured rate limit was exceeded.

get.summary: Verify an email address using an emailed token
get.description: Validates the latest verification credential for the user, with an expiry of 900 seconds after issuance. Superseded credentials are rejected as INVALID_TOKEN, even if their signatures and expiry are otherwise valid. The backend must atomically coordinate credential issuance and validation to enforce this project-specific rule. No signed-in session is required. The first successful verification records emailVerified=true and automatically creates or refreshes a login session through Set-Cookie; configure emailVerification.autoSignInAfterVerification=true and emailVerification.expiresIn=900. Without callbackURL, verification returns JSON; with a trusted callbackURL, it redirects on success or appends an error code on failure. The JSON user field may still be null; query /api/auth/get-session to load the session. Reopening a still-current link for an already-verified email does not guarantee a new session. An untrusted callback URL is rejected before token processing and is never used as a redirect target.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Latest verification credential issued for this user. It expires 900 seconds after issuance and is invalidated by any replacement verification link. This is not the session token.

parameters.name: callbackURL
parameters.description: Optional post-verification destination. May be a safe relative path or an absolute URL allowed by Better Auth's trusted-origin checks. A non-empty value selects redirect responses instead of JSON.

200.description: Latest credential accepted with no callback URL. First successful verification automatically establishes a login session. The user field may be null even after automatic sign-in; use get-session to load the session. An already-verified email may return success without creating a new session.

302.description: Redirect to the trusted callback URL. First successful verification automatically establishes a session before redirecting. Success keeps the destination; invalid or superseded credentials append error=INVALID_TOKEN, expired credentials append error=TOKEN_EXPIRED, and a missing user may append error=USER_NOT_FOUND. No JSON response body.

Location.description: Callback destination on success, or that destination with the verification error code appended on failure.

400.description: Missing required token or invalid query parameters; request validation failures are not callback redirects.

401.description: Verification failed without a callback URL: an invalid or superseded credential returns INVALID_TOKEN, a credential expired after 900 seconds returns TOKEN_EXPIRED, and a missing user returns USER_NOT_FOUND. This does not mean a signed-in session is required; no new session is created on failure.

403.description: The callback URL is not trusted. No redirect to the rejected URL is performed.

429.description: The configured rate limit was exceeded.

post.description: Button-triggered initial request or resend of a password-reset link. Requires emailAndPassword.sendResetPassword and emailAndPassword.resetPasswordTokenExpiresIn=900. Each issued reset credential expires 900 seconds after issuance. Issuing a replacement invalidates all earlier password-reset credentials for that user, while leaving verification credentials unaffected. The backend must enforce this latest-only rule atomically; Better Auth's default creation of independent reset records is insufficient. Do not expose whether the email belongs to an account. The default email link opens GET /api/auth/reset-password/{token}, which redirects to redirectTo with a token or error query parameter. The frontend then submits token and newPassword to POST /api/auth/reset-password. Issuing a link does not change the password or revoke sessions; all existing sessions are revoked only after the password reset succeeds. Resend cooldown and rate-limit values are not specified by this contract.

200.description: Request accepted without disclosing account existence. Any issued replacement credential is valid for 900 seconds and supersedes earlier reset credentials for that user; sessions are unchanged until a reset succeeds.

example.message: If this email exists in our system, check your email for the reset link

get.summary: Validate a password reset email link and redirect
get.description: Callback used by the password-reset email URL. No signed-in session is required. Checks that the credential is the user's latest password-reset credential, is unconsumed, and has not expired 900 seconds after issuance. Redirects to callbackURL with token on success or error=INVALID_TOKEN for invalid, superseded, expired, or consumed credentials. This GET does not consume the credential, extend its expiry, change the password, or revoke sessions. The frontend must submit token and newPassword to POST /api/auth/reset-password, which must repeat the authoritative latest-credential and expiry checks. Untrusted callback URLs are rejected before token processing. An empty callbackURL redirects to the auth base URL's /error page with error=INVALID_TOKEN.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Latest password-reset credential issued for this user. It expires 900 seconds after issuance and is invalidated by a replacement reset link.

parameters.name: callbackURL
parameters.description: Reset-password frontend destination, copied from request-password-reset's redirectTo by the default email URL. Use a safe relative path or an absolute URL allowed by trusted-origin checks. Supply a non-empty destination for the normal frontend flow; an empty value leads to the auth /error page.

302.description: Redirect to the reset-password page with token on success, or error=INVALID_TOKEN for an invalid, superseded, expired, or consumed credential. An empty callback URL redirects to the auth /error page. No JSON response body.

Location.description: Resolved callback URL with the token or error query parameter. Existing callback query parameters are retained.

400.description: Missing callbackURL or invalid callback query parameters; request validation failures are not redirect responses.

403.description: The callback URL is not trusted. No redirect to the rejected URL is performed.

429.description: The configured rate limit was exceeded.

post.description: Requires the user's latest unconsumed password-reset credential, valid for 900 seconds from issuance. Repeat the latest-credential and expiry checks even if the email-link GET callback previously accepted it; a resend or expiry between GET and POST must make the old credential fail. No signed-in session is required. Atomically validate and consume the credential, save the new password, and revoke all existing sessions for that user before reporting success; configure emailAndPassword.revokeSessionsOnPasswordReset=true and use transactional backend handling. Invalid, superseded, expired, or consumed credentials cannot change the password or revoke sessions. A successful reset does not create a new login session; all previous devices must sign in again. Protected APIs and get-session must check authoritative revocation state rather than accept stale cached sessions.

200.description: Password changed, current reset credential consumed, and all existing sessions revoked. No new session is created; sign in again.

400.description: Invalid request or invalid, superseded, expired after 900 seconds, or already-consumed reset credential. The password and sessions are unchanged on rejection.

post.description: Requires an authenticated Better Auth session and current password. Can revoke other sessions.

401.description: Authentication is required or session is invalid.

403.description: Action is prohibited or account is unverified.

post.description: Updates the current authenticated user profile (name and/or image).

401.description: Authentication is required or session is invalid.

get.description: Returns the active Better Auth sessions for the signed-in user.

401.description: Authentication is required or session is invalid.

post.description: Revokes a session owned by the current authenticated user using its session token.

401.description: Authentication is required or session is invalid.

200.description: A paginated list of the current user's applications.

put.description: Replace all client-editable fields of the application. Send a complete replacement representation: companyName, jobTitle and status are required. Omitted optional fields are cleared or reset to their defaults (for example, interviews becomes an empty array and resumeId becomes null). IDs and server timestamps cannot be changed.

200.description: A paginated list of the current user's resume metadata.

post.description: Accepts a PDF or DOCX resume as multipart/form-data.

Location.description: URL of the created resume metadata resource.

delete.description: Deletes the resume and its stored file. Applications referencing this resume are preserved and their resumeId is set to null.

200.description: Resume file content in its original format.

get.summary: List applications for AI position selection
get.description: Read the current user's existing active applications without creating workspaces, conversations, material snapshots, or model calls. Apply literal case-insensitive substring search to companyName or jobTitle and combine it with the optional status filter. Omit status for All. Use the same PRD matching rules as Application Management. An empty list supports the no-applications/no-matches UI and its route to Application Management.

200.description: List applications for AI position selection.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Literal company/position substring; an omitted or empty value applies no keyword filter. SQL wildcard characters are literals.

put.summary: Create or reuse an application workspace
put.description: Idempotently ensure the owned application's unique workspace exists, using the application uniqueness constraint under concurrent requests. Return 200 for both creation and reuse. No request body, detached project, conversation, material snapshot, or model call is created. Save pending application edits successfully before calling this entry action. The material metadata reflects saved application fields only.

200.description: Create or reuse an application workspace.

get.description: Read current header information and current material fingerprints and availability from the linked owned application. This does not snapshot material text into a conversation or synchronize any conversation. A changed application does not rebind existing conversations.
Return only this workspace's conversations. Listing never imports another conversation's history or calls the model.

post.description: Called only for an explicit New conversation action after selecting an application. No request body is needed. Create an immutable workspace binding with no messages, summaries, material snapshots, or generations; title and activeGenerationId are null and materialState is empty. Do not call the model or read materials into the conversation. Existing conversations remain unchanged.

get.description: Resolve ownership through conversation -> workspace -> application. Return the material baseline (the materials behind the latest completed answer) and any active attempt; this read does not refresh materials, start a model call, or expose internal compression text.

Return this conversation's full stored messages, including feedback, user-requested summaries, and optional website-tool records. Base-material loading creates no messages; the materials behind each answer are read through its generation. Internal compression does not replace this history. Reading history does not include another thread or initiate generation.

Read durable execution records for this conversation, including preparing, failed, and interrupted attempts. Use after reconnecting or losing the accepted event to inspect acceptance before resubmitting. It neither resumes a stream nor performs retry/deduplication.

post.summary: Send a message and stream a response
post.description: Accept a new user input and create one preparing attempt atomically after authorization. Only one preparing/streaming attempt may exist per conversation; an active conflict returns 409 without saving the rejected input. Backend code (not a model tool call) reads every material in the backend registry from one database snapshot, fingerprints each one, compares the fingerprints with the conversation's baseline (the latest completed generation), reuses saved snapshots with the same fingerprint, and atomically saves new snapshots, one association per registered kind, and the baseline reference before answer generation. All current material content is supplied with version labels in every request independently of history compression, together with a change notice when a baseline exists and materials changed. The core model request defines no tools; only the optional website tool may be offered. Missing materials allow limited assistance. Only a completed generation advances the baseline. Website-tool records, if any, and final replies are persisted in this conversation; complete answers and completed status commit together. No model or network wait occurs inside a database transaction. Errors before stream establishment use JSON HTTP responses. Once the response begins, failures use generation.error where possible; a dropped connection may have no terminal event. Do not treat EOF as completion or automatically repeat POST: read the generation or attempt list to reconcile durable state. Stream resumption/replay and request-key deduplication are not guaranteed by this contract. Retry/fallback/partial-output choices remain explicitly open.

get.description: Require the generation to belong to the authorized path conversation. Read status, input association, fixed materials, and saved final-message identity. A completed record proves final persistence; transport closure does not. Reading never starts another attempt or exposes operational lease/model secrets.

post.summary: Retry an interrupted or failed generation
post.description: Proposed contract pending the retry decisions in PRD section 11 and Database Design section 5.7. Resolve the path attempt within its conversation and retain its original user input; create a new attempt with a new identity and recheck current materials. Preserve the previous attempt and its saved material snapshots; a failed or interrupted attempt never advanced the baseline, so the new attempt repeats any change notice. No request body or client replacement history is accepted. Reuse the generation SSE transport. Eligibility, duplicate retry requests, key scope/retention, and partial-output handling must be agreed before this route is exposed; this description does not declare those rules approved.

409.description: The conversation has an active generation or the request is ineligible under the agreed retry policy; no new attempt is accepted.

error.message: The conversation has an active generation or the request is ineligible under the agreed retry policy; no new attempt is accepted.

get.summary: Read a saved conversation material snapshot
get.description: Require the snapshot to belong to the authorized path conversation. Return the immutable content and fingerprint actually supplied to the model, including explicit absence. This is historical provenance, not a live-material read, a download credential, or permission to relink a deleted resume. Snapshots remain readable with retained conversation history, including the text of a since-deleted resume, but never become current merely because this endpoint is called.

200.description: Read a saved conversation material snapshot.

VerificationSessionCookie.description: HttpOnly login-session cookie issued or refreshed after the first successful email verification. May be absent when reopening an already-verified link or when verification fails. Clients can use get-session to load the authenticated user even when the verification JSON contains user:null.

cookieAuth.name: better-auth.session_token
cookieAuth.description: Default Better Auth signed session cookie; cookie name/prefix may vary with production configuration.

bearerAuth.description: Optional Better Auth Bearer plugin. Send Authorization: Bearer <session-token>. This token is a Better Auth session token, not automatically a JWT. Enable the bearer plugin if this mode is needed.

ApplicationId.name: applicationId
ApplicationId.description: UUID of an application belonging to the authenticated user.

ResumeId.name: resumeId
ResumeId.description: UUID of a resume belonging to the authenticated user.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Maximum number of records returned per page.

AiWorkspaceId.name: workspaceId
AiWorkspaceId.description: Resource UUID. Validate ownership and all parent relationships in this route.

AiConversationId.name: conversationId
AiConversationId.description: Resource UUID. Validate ownership and all parent relationships in this route.

AiGenerationId.name: generationId
AiGenerationId.description: Resource UUID. Validate ownership and all parent relationships in this route.

AiSnapshotId.name: snapshotId
AiSnapshotId.description: Resource UUID. Validate ownership and all parent relationships in this route.

type.description: Interview stage, such as phone, technical, or final.

resumeId.description: Optional ID of the user's uploaded resume used for this application. Set to null to unlink a resume.

interviews.description: Full interview schedule. On PUT, this entire array replaces the existing schedule.

notes.description: Personal notes. Excluded from automatic AI base materials; use companyNotes for shared company background.

companyWebsiteUrl.description: Optional saved company website URL, separate from jobUrl. AI reads this URL as a base material; saving it does not fetch a webpage. Omission on full replacement clears it. Detailed URL validation remains open.

companyNotes.description: Optional company background notes shared by this application's conversations. Separate from personal notes. Omission on full replacement clears them.

ApplicationCreate.description: Application fields. Status defaults to saved when omitted.

name.description: Friendly name for the resume (e.g., Backend Developer Resume).

ApplicationReplace.description: Full replacement of client-editable application fields. Omitted optional fields are removed/reset rather than preserved.

callbackURL.description: Optional trusted post-verification destination included in the registration verification email link. Registration itself does not establish a login session.

BetterAuthUser.description: Core Better Auth user fields. Plugins may add fields.

BetterAuthSignUpResult.description: Registration response while email verification is required. No login session is created. Generic duplicate-email responses may use a synthetic user for enumeration protection.

token.description: Always null because registration does not establish a login session.

BetterAuthSignInResult.description: Successful email/password sign-in for an email-verified user. Registration uses the separate BetterAuthSignUpResult schema.

token.description: New session token. The browser login-session cookie is also set.
Sensitive session token; do not log or expose unnecessarily.

email.description: Email address to verify. With an active session, this must match the current user's unverified email address.

callbackURL.description: Optional safe relative path or trusted absolute URL to visit after verification. If omitted, Better Auth's generated verification link uses / as its callback.

status.description: True when the request is accepted; for anonymous requests this does not reveal account existence or guarantee email delivery.

user.description: May be null even when the first successful verification has automatically established a session. Use get-session to load that session. Reopening an already-verified link may also return null without creating a new session.

BetterAuthRequestPasswordResetResult.description: Generic acknowledgement for initial or repeated password-reset requests. Does not disclose whether the account exists or guarantee email delivery.

message.example: If this email exists in our system, check your email for the reset link

BetterAuthResetPasswordResult.description: Returned after saving the new password, consuming the current reset credential, and revoking every existing session for this user. Does not establish a new session; the user must sign in again.

redirectTo.description: Trusted reset-password frontend URL. Better Auth includes this destination as callbackURL in GET /api/auth/reset-password/{token}; that callback appends token on success or error=INVALID_TOKEN on failure. Supply this URL for the normal frontend flow; if omitted, the default email-link callback leads to the auth /error page.

token.description: Latest, unconsumed password-reset credential for the user, valid for 900 seconds from issuance. A replacement reset link immediately invalidates this credential.
Token of one of the current user sessions to revoke.

BetterAuthError.description: Better Auth error response, which is separate from custom API error format.

BetterAuthSuccess.description: Generic Better Auth success response. Fields can vary with library configuration.

AiRevision.description: Positive BIGINT revision or sequence encoded as a decimal string without precision loss.

AiApplicationStatus.description: Canonical PRD status for AI position selection; not the older ApplicationStatus enum.

AiApplicationOption.description: Projection of an existing owned application. Selection does not create another application or a conversation.

AiApplicationList.description: All matches in the current contract, newest application first with ID as a stable tie-breaker; an empty array means no matches. Pagination and limits remain open; do not silently truncate.

AiMaterialKind.description: Material kind identifier from the backend material registry. The current registry contains resume, jd, company, position, company_website_url, and company_notes. The set is defined by backend code, not by this contract's structure: clients must render kinds they do not recognize generically rather than reject them.

AiMaterialFingerprint.description: Opaque version identifier of one material: a scheme-versioned SHA-256 digest of the material's identity and exact content, or of its known absence. Equal fingerprints for the same kind mean the model was given the same material. Compare for equality only; it carries no ordering and is not derived from timestamps.

sourceResumeId.description: Resume library item the text came from; null for every other kind and for an unlinked resume. A historical identity only: it never authorizes file access.

reasonCode.description: Machine-readable reason for known absence, for example RESUME_NOT_LINKED or FIELD_MISSING; null when available. Read failures are not absence.

AiMaterialVersion.description: Current state of one application material, computed on read from saved application fields and the linked resume. No snapshot is created.

sourceResumeId.description: Resume library item the text came from; null for every other kind and for an unlinked resume. A historical identity only: it never authorizes file access.

reasonCode.description: Machine-readable reason for known absence, for example RESUME_NOT_LINKED or FIELD_MISSING; null when available. Read failures are not absence.

AiMaterialReference.description: A saved conversation-scoped snapshot fixed for a generation. Historical resume IDs do not authorize file access.

AiCurrentMaterials.description: One entry for every kind in the current material registry, including known absences. A map keyed by material kind; each entry's kind equals its key. The set of keys follows the backend material registry and is not fixed by this schema.

AiGenerationMaterials.description: One entry for every kind in the material registry when this generation's preparation committed, including known absences. A map keyed by material kind; each entry's kind equals its key. The set of keys follows the backend material registry and is not fixed by this schema.

AiConversationMaterialState.description: The conversation's baseline: the snapshots fixed for its latest completed generation. Derived, not separately stored. Empty before the first completed answer. It may lag current workspace materials until the next answer completes. A map keyed by material kind; each entry's kind equals its key. The set of keys follows the backend material registry and is not fixed by this schema.

AiLinkedResume.description: Current successful, non-deleted linked resume. No storage key or download credential is exposed.

AiWorkspace.description: Current application-backed workspace view. Material metadata is read without creating snapshots or advancing conversation sync state. Use the conversation-list route for independent threads.

AiConversation.description: Permanently bound to one workspace. title is nullable display metadata, not authorization for rename controls. Reading does not refresh materials or call the model.

AiConversationList.description: All conversations in the owned workspace, updatedAt descending then ID. No pagination limit is prescribed; no silent truncation.

AiFailure.description: Safe machine-readable failure and user-facing explanation; contains no credentials or private infrastructure details.

baselineGenerationId.description: Latest completed generation used as the comparison baseline; null for a conversation's first answer.

changedKinds.description: Kinds whose fingerprint differed from the baseline when preparation committed; null before preparation commits.

AiGeneration.description: Read-only attempt state. Preparing may have no snapshot. Failed/interrupted attempts retain any committed snapshot. streaming means preparation committed and generation is in progress; it does not guarantee a first text token. Internal leases, request keys, prompts, and provider configuration are not exposed. Only a completed generation becomes the conversation's baseline.

AiGenerationList.description: Persisted attempts for this conversation, startedAt descending then ID. Supports recovery if a connection is lost before the client receives the accepted event. No silent truncation or implicit retry.

sourceResumeId.description: Resume library item the text came from; null for every other kind and for an unlinked resume. A historical identity only: it never authorizes file access.

reasonCode.description: Machine-readable reason for known absence, for example RESUME_NOT_LINKED or FIELD_MISSING; null when available. Read failures are not absence.

generationId.description: Attempt whose preparation first saved this snapshot. Later generations may reuse it.

AiMaterialSnapshot.description: Immutable backend-saved material snapshot. Available snapshots contain exact historical text; unavailable snapshots contain no text. Snapshots of a deleted resume are retained as read-only history. Reading this record never rereads or restores a current application/resume.

AiToolCallPart.description: A genuine provider tool call. Used only by the optional website-reading tool; base materials never appear as tool calls. Tool arguments never establish ownership or override the authorized conversation scope, and the website host is derived from the authorized application.

AiWebsiteToolResult.description: Optional website-reading output, separate from company_website_url base material. An unchanged URL does not establish freshness. Website reading is not required for core acceptance.

AiToolResultPart.description: Result of a genuine provider call to the optional website-reading tool.

role.description: tool is used only by the optional website-reading tool.

AiMessage.description: Persisted application message format, not raw provider JSON. User inputs have no generationId; attempts reference them using inputMessageId. Assistant and website-tool records belong to their attempt. Base-material loading creates no messages. Feedback and user-requested summaries are ordinary assistant messages. Internal compression summaries and system prompts are not returned.

AiMessageList.description: Full persisted history ordered by numeric sequenceNo ascending; decimal strings must not be sorted lexicographically. Compression never removes these records. In-flight text deltas are not proof of persisted messages; partial-output policy remains open. Pagination is not prescribed and history must not be silently truncated.

content.description: Actual user input after any shortcut editing. Whitespace-only input is invalid; length limits remain open.

AiSendMessage.description: Only a new user text is accepted. Do not accept caller-supplied roles, history, material contents/versions, model settings, workspace IDs, or system prompts. The server derives context from the authorized conversation.

AiGenerationAcceptedEvent.description: Emitted after the accepted user input and preparing attempt commit. For a proposed explicit retry, inputMessage is the previously persisted user input. It is not evidence of material synchronization or successful answer generation.

baselineGenerationId.description: Latest completed generation used as the comparison baseline; null for a conversation's first answer.

AiMaterialSyncEvent.description: Emitted only after atomic preparation commits. changedKinds lists kinds whose fingerprint differs from the baseline, including a kind present on only one side: with no baseline every kind is first-time; it is empty when nothing changed since the latest completed answer. The model receives a change notice only when a baseline exists and changedKinds is non-empty. A saved reference for every registered kind remains present. Display sync/absence notices without labeling missing materials as supplied text.

AiTextDeltaEvent.description: Append text in received order. Deltas are provisional until generation.completed; do not count them as saved messages.

AiGenerationCompletedEvent.description: Terminal success emitted only after the final answer and completed status commit atomically. message.id matches generation.assistantMessageId, and message.generationId matches generation.id.

AiGenerationErrorEvent.description: Terminal failure notification, not a success marker. statePersisted=false means the durable terminal state is unavailable or uncertain; query generation status before retrying. Error codes include MATERIAL_REFRESH_FAILED, CONTEXT_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED, GENERATION_FAILED, GENERATION_INTERRUPTED, and MESSAGE_PERSISTENCE_FAILED. This event does not select a refresh fallback or partial-output policy.

EmailNotVerified.description: The session's user has not verified their email. Protected business operations require both a valid session and a currently verified email.

error.message: Verify your email before accessing this resource.

BadRequest.description: Invalid request body or query parameters.

Unauthorized.description: No valid Better Auth session was supplied.

NotFound.description: Resource not found or not owned by the authenticated user.

UnsupportedMediaType.description: Uploaded file type is not supported. Only PDF and DOCX are allowed.

ValidationError.description: Valid JSON, but field values or referenced resume are invalid.

AiGenerationConflict.description: Another generation is active in this conversation. No new user input or attempt is accepted; other conversations remain available.

error.message: Another generation is active in this conversation. No new user input or attempt is accepted; other conversations remain available.

AiServiceUnavailable.description: AI persistence or execution infrastructure is unavailable before a stream is established. No successful generation is implied; query saved attempts if request acceptance is uncertain.

error.message: AI persistence or execution infrastructure is unavailable before a stream is established. No successful generation is implied; query saved attempts if request acceptance is uncertain.

AiGenerationStream.description: An SSE stream. Each frame has event: <type> and data: <one JSON AiStreamEvent>, followed by a blank line; event and data.type must match. Order: generation.accepted, then materials.synced after preparation, zero or more text.delta events, then generation.completed or generation.error. Preparation failure may go directly from accepted to error. No success event precedes final database commit. Network loss may omit the terminal event. Use a streaming POST client; these custom events require an SDK adapter.

Cache-Control.description: Private conversation content must not be cached.

preparationFailure.summary: Accepted input followed by a reported preparation failure; the fail-and-retry fallback is proposed pending policy resolution.

completedWithMissingMaterials.summary: Successful limited assistance with only company and position available; completion follows durable answer persistence.

requirements: PRD.md 1.4: FR-02, FR-10 through FR-20, FR-25, FR-27 through FR-30, FR-34, FR-35
x-ai-design.authorization: Resolve user -> application -> workspace -> conversation -> generation/snapshot on the server for every operation. A valid session and current verified email are mandatory. Return 404 for missing, inaccessible, or mismatched resource chains without disclosing another owner. Model arguments and client-supplied history cannot widen this boundary.
x-ai-design.context: Every model request uses the fixed structure in AI Design section 4.2: system rules, all current base materials with version labels from the generation's fixed snapshots, a change notice when materials differ from the baseline, this conversation's usable compressed history, recent messages (annotated when based on superseded versions), and the current input exactly once. Base materials never depend on the history window. Only superseded or removed materials are historical-only. Summaries never replace base materials or delete full history.
x-ai-design.materialUpdates: Application/resume operations own current materials; AI routes are read-only with respect to those sources and require no version counters from them. Backend code, not a model tool, fingerprints each registered material (identity plus exact content, or its known absence) and compares the fingerprints with the baseline (latest completed generation). Reuse snapshots with a matching fingerprint, save new ones otherwise, and freeze one snapshot per registered kind before generating. An edit that is reverted before the next turn is not a change. Only completion advances the baseline. Missing materials permit limited assistance; infrastructure read failures are distinct. Edits during generation apply to a later snapshot.
x-ai-design.streaming: The documented SSE events are an application transport contract. Use an explicit adapter for the selected Vercel AI SDK integration; these event names are not claimed to be its native UI-message wire protocol.
openDecisions: Retry deduplication: request-key scope, payload mismatch, retention, and eligibility; the retry operation is a proposed contract and must not be exposed before these decisions are resolved.
Partial assistant-output persistence and transport-disconnection handling; do not infer that EOF cancels or completes a generation.
Explicit refresh-error fallback; Database Design proposes visible failure and retry rather than stale-material generation.
Model/provider, website-tool step limits (if implemented), timeouts, summary thresholds/window, and oversized-base-material handling; do not silently discard current materials.
Pagination/limits, conversation rename/delete, and application deletion/chat retention remain governed by PRD section 11.
integrationDependencies: The AI application selector is a read projection of existing applications, not a separate project store. It uses the six PRD statuses and literal case-insensitive company/position search. The older non-AI ApplicationStatus contract still requires separate alignment; do not reuse its incompatible enum or silently map legacy values.
Company website URL and company notes are added to ApplicationFields to support editing the approved AI material sources. Other non-AI endpoint discrepancies are outside this AI contract revision.
Use only a successfully parsed, non-deleted linked PDF as a current resume. Never trust the older upload contract as authorization to use an unsupported or unparsed file for AI.

No public endpoint edits material snapshots or the baseline, runs compression directly, overwrites history, or exposes system prompts, leases, storage keys, or model credentials. Website reading remains optional; no separate mock-interview state machine or report API is introduced.
